assessments.technical_explanation: The serialize-environment signal corresponds to passing the inherited process environment to a child process spawned via execFileSync with fully fixed, literal arguments. This is the standard and necessary way to run local npm scripts, and it neither serializes environment contents into a persistent artifact nor transmits them anywhere. All child invocations target locally defined repomix build commands; no external endpoints, obfuscated strings, or credential-shaped data are present in the supplied source.
assessments.layman_explanation: When the script runs local build commands, it hands them the same environment settings every command-line program normally gets. This is routine plumbing, not a way to copy or leak secret settings; the environment is not saved to disk or sent out.
assessments.developer_action: none

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged signal corresponds to reading one configuration value from the environment and passing the inherited environment to child processes spawned with fixed, literal arguments. This is a pre-commit hook that runs type checking, formatting, linting, and tests locally on the developer's machine. It performs no network requests, writes no data outside the repository and git index, and serializes no environment contents anywhere. All executed commands are locally defined package scripts.
assessments.layman_explanation: This is the project author's own pre-commit checklist: it runs the type checker, formatter, and tests before each commit.
